item.title: Braves edge Brewers in Little League Classic
item.description: Tyler Mahle threw five solid innings to continue his impressive run and Michael Harris II homered to help the Atlanta Braves post a 4-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Tyler Mahle threw five solid innings to continue his impressive run and Michael Harris II homered to help the Atlanta Braves post a 4-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in the MLB Little League Classic in Williamsport, Pa. Mahle (5-10) allowed one run on six hits while striking out four and walking two. Mahle has a 1.52 ERA in four starts since being traded from the San Francisco Giants. Raisel Iglesias earned a four-out save for Atlanta, which had dropped five of its last six games. Milwaukee starter Shane Drohan (6-5) threw five innings and allowed two runs and eight hits. He struck out five and walked three for the Brewers, who had won six of their last seven. Iglesias allowed a leadoff single to Jackson Chourio and walked Brice Turang to begin the bottom of the ninth. After William Contreras flew out to the warning track, Iglesias began a 1-6-3 double play against Jake Bauers to secure his 27th save in 30 tries. In the top of the second, Ozzie Albies and Lane Thomas singled before Mauricio Dubon slashed a ground-rule double to give the Braves a 1-0 edge. Milwaukee tied the game in the third, as Turang singled and scored on Bauers' RBI base hit. Atlanta's Drake Baldwin doubled to begin the fourth and Thomas followed that with his second single to place runners at the corners. Drohan retired the next two batters, but Sean Murphy legged out an infield single to give the Braves a 2-1 lead. Grant Anderson spelled Drohan in the sixth and allowed Dubon's one-out walk and Austin Riley's single. After he struck out Murphy, DL Hall entered as the Brewers' second reliever of the inning. Atlanta doubled its lead as Harris' soft grounder to first was bobbled by Andrew Vaughn and allowed Dubon to score. Mahle began the bottom of the sixth, but Vaughn led off with a single and Christian Yelich reached on Matt Olson's throwing error. Didier Fuentes then entered and got Joey Ortiz to ground into a double play before Luis Lara's groundout ended the threat. Lara had replaced Garrett Mitchell, who left with a forearm contusion after being hit by a pitch in the fourth. Fuentes threw two scoreless innings in relief. Dylan Lee relieved Fuentes in the eighth and surrendered a double to Yelich and a two-out triple by Lara, cutting the Brewers' deficit to 3-2. Iglesias entered and retired Gary Sanchez to strand Lara at third. Harris connected on his 21st homer of the season to give Atlanta an insurance run in the top of the ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Miyu Yamashita rolls to 9-shot win in Canada, ties LPGA scoring record
item.description: Miyu Yamashita tied an LPGA Tour scoring record as she sailed to a nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open on Sunday in Edmonton.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Miyu Yamashita tied an LPGA Tour scoring record as she sailed to a nine-shot victory at the CPKC Women's Open on Sunday in Edmonton. Yamashita was ahead by six shots after the third round and carded a 4-under-par 66 Sunday to finish at 23-under 257 for the week at Royal Mayfair Golf Club. Yuri Yoshida of Japan was a distant second at 14 under par after a 69. Not only did the rising star from Japan collect her fourth LPGA victory in 13 months, her 257 tied the tour's 72-hole record for the lowest gross score of all time. She capped that with a triumphant birdie putt on the par-4 18th hole, closing a round of six birdies and two bogeys. "I was nervous, nervous round, so my shot, my game, I trust my swing," Yamashita, 25, said on the TV broadcast. Yamashita broke through in August 2025 when she claimed her first major, the AIG Women's Open, which doubled as her first win in an official LPGA Tour event. Before that, she racked up 13 titles on the LPGA of Japan Tour. She opened the week with rounds of 62 and 64 to create plenty of space between her and the field. Yoshida's highlight was an eagle at the par-5 12th hole amid one birdie and two bogeys. She said she was looking forward to the schedule's upcoming Asian Swing, which will see the LPGA play in China, South Korea, Malaysia and Japan across October and November. "Hopefully, I can play Asian Swing, right, so I'm happy to play Asian Swing and I'm really excited to play next week, too," she said. Sei Young Kim of South Korea shot a 67 and placed third at 13 under. The low Canadian was 17-year-old Anna Huang, whose final-round 65 boosted her into a tie for fourth at 12 under with Gina Ki (71) and China's Ruoning Yin (68). Huang, a native of Vancouver, has been a revelation on the Ladies European Tour, where she's won four times since last September, most recently the PIF London Championship earlier this month. "I think always like to make a cut at any LPGA event is really special," Huang said. "And then to play so well as I did this week at the Canadian Open is just really, really awesome I guess. And, yeah, I'm really happy that I played well in front of the best in the world and, hopefully, I can continue doing that." Another rising star from Canada, 16-year-old amateur Aphrodite Deng, followed her Saturday 63 with a 69 and tied for seventh at 11 under with Laney Frye (68) and Thailand's Ariya Jutanugarn (68). --Field Level Media

item.title: Rupee set for quiet open, supported by inflows; oil, month-end activity eyed
item.description: The Indian rupee is poised for a quiet start to the week, buoyed by robust capital inflows, while traders keep an eye on oil prices and anticipated interventions by the central bank to keep the currency on a steady footing.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is poised for a quiet start to the week, buoyed by robust capital inflows, while traders keep an eye on oil prices and anticipated interventions by the central bank to keep the currency on a steady footing. The rupee is expected to open in the 95.65-95.70 range, per traders, having settled at 95.6950 to the dollar on Friday. Oil prices slipped on Monday as investors awaited an expected announcement from Washington about imposing [USN:L1N44K05C TEXT:"more sanctions"] on Iran that may further disrupt energy supplies from the Middle East. U.S. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners. Uncertainty over the conflict could keep risk appetite curtailed but pressure on the rupee is expected to be offset by the Reserve Bank of India's presence in the market, similar to the last two weeks. Over the weekend, the central bank said it has garnered nearly $73 billion under measures rolled out in June to strengthen India's balance of payments, helping lift [USN:L4N44I0QN TEXT:"FX reserves"] just shy of a record high. "We expect the RBI to use inflows to reduce its FX forward book and/or rebuild FX reserves, rather than allow a material appreciation of the currency," analysts at Goldman Sachs said in a note. The firm has revised its three-, six- and 12-month rupee forecasts weaker to 96,97,97 from 94,95,96, respectively, after the RBI brought forward the closure of the discounted hedging facility for overseas deposits by a month. Elsewhere, Asian currencies and stocks were mostly rangebound, with investors awaiting results from chip major Nvidia (NVDA.O) later this week followed by a key speech from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday.

item.title: Indian food safety officer shakes up Mumbai, one viral raid at a time
item.description: Tukaram Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission.
item.dc:creator: Arpan Chaturvedi, Vibhuti Sharma, Dhwani Pandya
item.content:encoded: Tukaram Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission. As a state food safety commissioner, the 51-year-old has raided food businesses in the country's commercial capital Mumbai in an unprecedented crackdown on poor hygiene and unsafe food that has captivated the public nationwide. Mundhe has led the suspension of food permits of [USN:L4N44B0ID TEXT:"four Domino's and one Pizza Hut"] outlet in recent weeks, and has also targeted cricket clubs, hotels and well-known restaurants in over 3,000 raids since he took over as Maharashtra's food safety chief in May. When a Mumbai judge accused Mundhe of selective aggression towards private outlets and asked if court canteens were checked, his teams conducted inspections there within hours, shutting some of them which operated without licenses. "Those who try to not comply, they will face what is expected from the regulator," Mundhe said in an interview with Reuters, talking about his no-nonsense approach. "You are dealing with the lives of people." Mundhe has won widespread public admiration across India because he has tapped into deep public frustration. Even though foreign chains such as Domino's (DPZ.O) and McDonald's (MCD.N) are fast expanding, it is local eateries, roadside kiosks and small restaurants — long dogged by concerns over hygiene — that remain hugely popular. Each year since 2020, Indian food inspectors have checked more than 100,000 food samples and found roughly 20% to be unsafe, substandard or lacking proper labels, government data shows. Nearly 8,000 food business licenses have been cancelled in the last three years. "Everyone has tried to normalise this for years by saying it happens in India. It's basically bottled-up anger," said Ankur Bisen, a partner at consumer consulting firm The Knowledge Company. "I have never seen anyone like Mundhe. It's giving people hope." FINDING RATS AND EXPIRED FOOD Mundhe, who is bespectacled and sports a chevron moustache, has an unconventional operating style. He has featured in TV interviews declaring nobody dare bribe him, and that he is not afraid of administrative action despite being transferred numerous times in his 21-year career as an officer of the highly regarded Indian Administrative Service. "I get transferred every year," he said in a 2018 interview. Now, his food safety team's actions go viral daily — raids lead to detailed public statements and graphic images that show interiors of eateries and [USN:L4N44C017 TEXT:"grocery warehouses"] with stained walls, crawling cockroaches and rats, and even expired food — photos that have shocked many Indians. "It was surprising. I did not expect these many violations," Mundhe said. In Mumbai, Reuters visits last week to 25 street vendors and restaurants showed heightened fear about Mundhe's raids. One vendor has swapped artificial red dye for natural chilli in Chinese offerings, while another has started changing his frying oil three times a day and requires staff to wear gloves and head caps. Mumbai's omnipresent street food 'vada pav' — a spicy potato patty in a bun — has not escaped Mundhe's attention. In June, he prohibited use of newspapers as packaging material — often used to wrap the delicacy. Customers are noticing the change and consuming street food more confidently. Supriya Wagle, 14, is happy her favourite vada pav is now being packed in cleaner butter paper, saying that is "surely a relief". CRITICISM AMID CELEBRITY STATUS After finding lapses at some Domino's and Pizza Hut stores, Mundhe's team on Friday suspended the permit of a McDonald's outlet after finding "live pest activity (cockroaches)" and "rotting food". The three companies did not respond to Reuters queries. Mundhe's crackdown has included action against a Mumbai British-era cricket club, a 70-year-old ice cream parlour and a 110-year-old Parsi Dairy. He is facing criticism from businesses that say they should be given time to adapt, with some approaching the High Court and accusing his department of high-handedness. In one case, the judges fined his department 500,000 rupees ($5,225) for continued suspension of an eatery even though it improved its compliance. "If there are observations by the court, we take it seriously ... if there is scope for improvement, we improve," Mundhe said. At an event in New Delhi on Friday, fans clicked quick selfies with Mundhe and jostled to shake his hand. One fan told him Prime Minister Narendra Modi should give him a national role. "I don't think I'm a celebrity. I'm just a food safety commissioner," he told Reuters.

item.title: North Korea preparing further Russia troop deployments, no sign move imminent, Seoul says
item.description: South Korea's Defence Ministry said North Korea was continuing preparations for an additional troop deployment to Russia, but had detected no signs that such a deployment was imminent, according to a South Korean lawmaker's office.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korea's Defence Ministry said North Korea was continuing preparations for an additional troop deployment to Russia, but had detected no signs that such a deployment was imminent, according to a South Korean lawmaker's office. The assessment came after North Korea's [USN:L1N44G0IC TEXT:"Kim Yo Jong"], sister of leader Kim Jong Un, last week denied Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's claim that Pyongyang planned to send up to 50,000 more troops to Russia to fight for its ally. South Korea's Defence Ministry said in a statement to lawmaker Yu Yong-weon that North Korea had continued to supply Russia with weapons systems, including short-range ballistic missiles, according to Yu's office. North Korea is estimated to have supplied Russia with more than 15 million rounds of artillery ammunition, measured in 152-millimetre shell equivalents, it said. The lawmaker's office, citing a South Korean Defense Intelligence Agency assessment, said North Korean missiles used in the war may have improved in accuracy through battlefield data, alongside Russian technical advice and component support. The ministry also said the development of some North Korean ballistic missiles and multiple rocket launchers assessed as being intended for use in a conflict with South Korea was nearing completion, the lawmaker's office said. The ministry added that North Korea's Hwasong-12 intermediate-range ballistic missile, capable of reaching the U.S. territory of Guam, was being prepared for operational deployment, according to Yu's office. North Korea's intercontinental ballistic missiles have the flight capability to reach the U.S. mainland, the ministry said, but key technologies, including warhead re-entry, have not been verified because all test launches have been conducted on lofted trajectories. North Korea and Russia have deepened military cooperation since Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with Pyongyang supplying artillery ammunition and missiles since 2023 and deploying troops from 2024, according to South Korean, Ukrainian and Western assessments. Moscow and Pyongyang have previously denied arms transfers.

item.title: Indian shares likely to open higher; caution ahead of new Iran sanctions
item.description: Indian shares were expected to open marginally higher on Monday, following two consecutive weekly losses, although sentiment will remain cautious as investors await details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran later in the session.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian shares were expected to open marginally higher on Monday, following two consecutive weekly losses, although sentiment will remain cautious as investors await details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran later in the session. GIFT Nifty futures were at 24,378 points, as of 7:47 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index (.NSEI) , which closed at 24,252 on Friday. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference at 1800 GMT on Monday, after threatening to impose "the [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"toughest sanctions"] in history" on Iran. Iran's foreign minister dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation on Sunday and said the expected new measures would fail to defeat Tehran. The nearly six-month-old war between the U.S. and Iran has led to a surge in energy prices globally, driving inflation fears. India, which is the third-largest global crude importer, has seen record foreign investor outflows from equities earlier this year, largely due to higher crude prices. The Nifty 50 and the BSE Sensex (.BSESN) shed 0.5% and 0.6%, respectively, last week, as higher crude oil prices and bond yields due to an escalating Middle East war weighed on sentiment. This was their second consecutive week of losses. "Persistent Middle East tensions and elevated crude oil prices continue to temper risk appetite," said Ponmudi R, chief executive officer of Enrich Money. Brent crude futures were down 2% but remained elevated at $93 per barrel, after a 13% jump in the last two weeks. Asian markets were flat as investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran and Nvidia (NVDA.O) results later this week, while the Canadian dollar dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour. item.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine not behind Nord Stream blasts, cooperating with probe
item.description: Ukraine played no role in blowing up the Nord Stream gas pipelines and is cooperating with an investigation into the matter, President Volodymyr Zelenksiy said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine played no role in blowing up the Nord Stream gas pipelines and is cooperating with an investigation into the matter, President Volodymyr Zelenksiy said on Sunday. "Ukraine has never officially taken part in any operations regarding the blowing up of the Nord Stream 2 pipeline," he told reporters in Kyiv. The Nord Stream 1 and 2 natural gas pipelines between Russia and Germany were damaged in explosions in September 2022, and two Ukrainian suspects are currently in custody on suspicion of involvement.

item.title: Shein pourrait atteindre une valorisation de $27 mds lors de son IPO à Hong Kong
item.description: La valorisation de Shein a chuté d'environ 70% par rapport au pic de près de 100 milliards de dollars atteint lors d'un tour de table effectué il y a quatre ans, alors que le géant en ligne chinois de la mode éphémère entend lever jusqu'à 1,77 milliards de dollars en vue de son introduction en Bourse à Hong Kong.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La valorisation de Shein a chuté d'environ 70% par rapport au pic de près de 100 milliards de dollars atteint lors d'un tour de table effectué il y a quatre ans, alors que le géant en ligne chinois de la mode éphémère entend lever jusqu'à 1,77 milliards de dollars en vue de son introduction en Bourse à Hong Kong. D'après des documents déposés lundi, Shein propose 280 millions d'actions à un prix unitaire compris entre 47,60 et 49,50 dollars hongkongais, ce qui valorise le groupe à près de 27 milliards de dollars américains en tenant compte du haut de la fourchette. Il s'agit d'un montant en forte baisse par rapport à des tours de table effectués en 2022, qui valorisaient alors Shein à 98,2 milliards de dollars. La société était valorisée à 64 milliards de dollars en 2023 puis en avril 2024. Comme rapporté la semaine dernière, Shein entrera en cotation le 1er septembre. L'entreprise a fait savoir qu'elle annoncerait la veille le prix final de ses actions. Plus tôt cet été, quand il a débuté des réunions avec des investisseurs en vue de son IPO, le géant de la 'fast fashion' visait une valorisation comprise entre 30 milliards et 40 milliards de dollars. Mais le groupe a fait face à des interrogations sur sa croissance, qui a connu un ralentissement, sur la hausse de ses coûts et sur l'évolution des conditions du marché. Des investisseurs ont dit par le passé ne pas être convaincus que Shein puisse retrouver les taux de croissance qui justifiaient il y a quatre ans une valorisation de près de 100 milliards de dollars. Selon le prospectus communiqué lundi par Shein, les investisseurs de référence, au premier rang desquels les actionnaires existants Boyu, Tiger Global et General Atlantic, ont souscrit à environ 383 millions de dollars d'actions. Tencent (0700.HK) , Greenwoods, Taikang Life et UBS Asset Management vont également acquérir des actions. Le géant chinois a déclaré qu'il utiliserait environ 80% des fonds levés lors de son IPO pour améliorer sa technologie et renforcer sa marque ainsi que sa présence mondiale. D'après les documents, il s'est engagé à verser jusqu'à environ 3,5 milliards de dollars en espèces à certains investisseurs ayant acquis des actions spéciales lors de précédents tours de table privés. Les actions vendues lors de l'IPO à Hong Kong attribueront un dixième des droits de vote des actions détenues par les fondateurs de la société. Les cofondateurs Sky Yangtian Xu, Maggie Gu, Molly Miao et Tony Ren contrôleront 90% des droits de vote de Shein, est-il indiqué également.

item.title: Man suspected of murdering five in Oregon found dead
item.description: A man suspected of killing five people in rural Oregon was found dead in a suspected suicide, local law enforcement said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A man suspected of killing five people in rural Oregon was found dead in a suspected suicide, local law enforcement said on Sunday. The deceased individuals were found on Saturday at a home in a rural community near Forest Grove, Oregon, around 30 miles (48 km) outside Portland, when authorities responded to a report of a vehicle fire. An unspecified number of domesticated animals were also found deceased at the home, authorities said. "In my 22 years here, I have not been a part of or witnessed a scene quite this complex," said Caprice Massey, the sheriff in Washington County, Oregon, where the alleged killings occurred. The Washington County Sheriff's Office identified 36-year-old Benjamin Charles Parker as the suspect. Local police found Parker dead in his vehicle in Enumclaw, Washington, around 45 miles outside Seattle. He is believed to have died by suicide, they said.

item.title: Alibaba shares fall 8% after $10 billion Hong Kong share sale
item.description: Alibaba shares fell 8% in early Hong Kong trade on Monday after the tech company finalised a HK$80 billion ($10.21 billion) share placement at HK$112.70 apiece, in a deal aimed at funding artificial intelligence-related development.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alibaba (9988.HK) shares fell 8% in early Hong Kong trade on Monday after the tech company finalised a HK$80 billion ($10.21 billion) share placement at HK$112.70 apiece, in a deal aimed at funding artificial intelligence-related development. The Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing company priced 710 million new shares at an 8.4% discount to the last close of its Hong Kong-listed stock. The deal is the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company and the third-largest globally this year after offerings by [USN:L4N4291N6 TEXT:"Alphabet"] (GOOGL.O) and [USN:L6N4470KC TEXT:"Intel"] (INTC.O) . Alibaba intends to use proceeds to fund AI development, including the expansion of related infrastructure. The share placement comes a week after Alibaba reported quarterly earnings in which it said it had already spent nearly half of its three-year capital expenditure plan. It brought forward its projected payback on AI investment to two and a half years from three due to surging demand for AI services. Its [USN:L4N44H0OB TEXT:"quarterly net profit"] fell 75% from a year earlier due primarily to AI-related spending. Last week, digital technology and AI division Alibaba Cloud launched its third data centre in South Korea , bringing its network to 104 availability zones across 30 regions. The move was a part of Alibaba's AI infrastructure pledge, announced in October, [USN:L5N3VU0SZ TEXT:"to invest 380 billion yuan"] ($56.54 billion) over three years. item.title: Dollar trading near multi-month lows, restrained by debt nerves
item.description: A wavering dollar teetered near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the U.S. Treasury's promise to buy back more long bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the U.S. and Japan.
item.dc:creator: Tom Westbrook
item.content:encoded: A wavering dollar teetered near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the U.S. Treasury's promise to buy back more long bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the U.S. and Japan. The Canadian dollar slipped 0.2% in early trade, to C$1.3798 per dollar, after trade talks with the U.S. collapsed and Washington imposed [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"50% tariffs on Canadian goods"], with Canada retaliating in kind. The Australian and New Zealand dollars traded just shy of three-month highs at $0.7171 and $0.5979 respectively. The euro was comfortably above $1.16 at $1.1685 while the yen kept to the strong side of 159 per dollar. Friday data showing the strongest [USN:ZON00GDKK TEXT:"U.S. services growth"] in nearly two years in August held off dollar sellers in steady early trade. The dollar logged its largest weekly drop against bitcoin in nearly three-and-a-half years on Sunday and it's been sliding sharply on gold over [USN:L1N44H0RB TEXT:"revived fears the currency will suffer"] if the U.S. tries to hold down yields. Long-end yields have been [USN:L1N44F086 TEXT:"climbing globally"] on a combination of a solid economic growth outlook, rising inflation expectations and nerves about [USN:L6N44G17Z TEXT:"ballooning sovereign debts"]. Last week, after 30-year yields hit almost two-decade highs, the U.S. Treasury announced it would [USN:L1N44G0GD TEXT:"double buybacks"] at the long end to $4 billion per operation. The size is paltry in a market worth $32 trillion but the interventionist signal spooked traders and hit the dollar. "The U.S. Treasury's attempts to artificially hold down long-term bond yields appears to be reigniting the $US debasement trade," said Shane Oliver, head of investment strategy at Australian financial services firm AMP. The mood was keeping Australian dollar above 71 cents, he said. Sterling was firm at $1.3650 in morning trade and the yuan , which notched an eighth straight weekly rise last week, hovered near a 3/1-2 year high at 6.7222 per dollar. SANCTIONS AND WARSH Later on Monday, at 1800 GMT, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to hold a press conference after threatening "[USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"the toughest sanctions in history"]" on Iran, with markets focused on whether he will target [USN:L6N44H0PZ TEXT:"China"]. Iran's foreign minister has dismissed the threat of new U.S. sanctions as a sign of desperation. Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday. He is also sure to face questions about Treasury's buybacks. "Any comments on the balance sheet, duration supply, or term premium could move the long end more than the data itself. That said, given Warsh’s typically restrained style, we aren’t holding our breath," said BNY strategist Geoff Yu. A Thursday appearance by Bank of Japan deputy governor Ryozo Himino will also be closely watched as a prelude to next month's policy meeting. In particular, investors will be looking to see if he pushes back on a shift in market pricing to see a faster pace of hikes. "Himino may signal the BOJ is moving closer to another interest rate hike," said Commonwealth Bank of Australia strategist Joe Capurso. "However, any hawkish comments are likely to exert only modest downward pressure on USD/JPY. Developments in the U.S. bond market area are a more important driver of USD/JPY."

item.title: Inflow cushion to anchor rupee against month-end flows; bonds track oil, Treasuries
item.description: The Indian rupee is likely to be rangebound this week as robust capital inflows, supported by policy measures, help contain volatility, while government bonds may face headwinds as markets focus on oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields.
item.dc:creator: Dharamraj Dhutia, Jaspreet Kalra
item.content:encoded: The Indian rupee is likely to be rangebound this week as robust capital inflows, supported by policy measures, help contain volatility, while government bonds may face headwinds as markets focus on oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields. The rupee closed nearly flat at 95.6950 on Friday, down about 0.3% week-on-week but avoiding steeper losses on account of sustained interventions by the Reserve Bank of India. Over the weekend, the central bank said it has garnered [USN:L4N44J00P TEXT:"nearly $73 billion"] under measures rolled out in June to strengthen India's balance of payments, helping boost the country's [USN:L4N44I0QN TEXT:"FX reserves"] in striking distance of their record high. Bankers and analysts say inflows have bolstered the central bank's ammunition to anchor the currency, which is expected to persist this week. "Market participants want to position long Dollars but are fearing RBI presence around 95.80. Interbank activity and participation therefore seemed muted," FX advisory firm IFA Global said in a note. Month-end flows related to derivative maturities and corporate payments are among the factors, which could strain the rupee this week alongside still elevated oil prices due to Iran war. After nearly [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"six months of war"] since the U.S. and Israel launched airstrikes against Iran on February 28, the sides are not firing at each other but also showing no sign of pursuing peace talks. Outcomes of central bank policy reviews in South Korea, the Philippines and Thailand will also be in focus as policymakers navigate inflationary pressures and volatility spurred by the Middle East conflict. BONDS Government bonds are likely to trade in a narrow range, after the benchmark bond yield witnessed its sharpest weekly rise so far this financial year in the previous week, crossing the crucial level of 6.85%. The 10-year bond yield ended at 6.8495% on Friday, up 9 basis points, the biggest spike since the week ended April 3, after falling an aggregate of 7 basis points in the previous two weeks. Traders expect the benchmark yield to move in the 6.80% to 6.89% range, with a trading holiday on Wednesday and commentary from Fed officials on Thursday-Friday. The minutes of RBI's latest meeting released on Wednesday showed policymakers are open to rate hikes, if inflation risks materialise and broaden. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said that evidence of such spillovers could warrant "policy tightening", while Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said a case for a hike may emerge this year. The benchmark Brent crude contract gained nearly 7% last week and was around $94 per barrel mark, a concern for India's inflation outlook. The focus would also remain on foreign investors after India was not included in a global index on July 31. "The delay does not change India's structural story, and other factors, such as the strong inflows into the non-resident scheme, could provide near-term support," said Shamaila Khan, head of fixed income for emerging markets and Asia-Pacific at UBS Asset Management. item.title: Alibaba stock slumps in Hong Kong after $10.2 billion share placement to fund AI
item.description: The Hong Kong-listed shares of Alibaba slumped on Monday after the Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing company launched a $10.2 billion share placement, as investors worried about payback from its massive AI spending.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Hong Kong-listed shares of Alibaba (9988.HK) slumped on Monday after the Chinese e-commerce and cloud computing company launched a $10.2 billion share placement, as investors worried about payback from its massive AI spending. Alibaba said on Sunday its HK$80 billion ($10.21 billion) share [USN:L6N44K00V TEXT:"placement"] finalised at HK$112.70 apiece – an 8.4% discount to its Friday close – is aimed at funding AI-related development, as it redoubles AI bets amid competition and simmering Sino-U.S. tech rivalry. Its shares fell as much as 10% to HK$110.10 in early Hong Kong trade. "It's negative news in the short-term ... as the share placement dilutes shareholders' interest," said Charles Wang, chairman of Shenzhen Dragon Pacific Capital Management. "In addition, investors generally don't like capex ... though the investment is beneficial in the long term." The view echoes concern in the U.S. where investors increasingly question when massive AI spending will generate returns. The deal is the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company and the third-largest globally this year after offerings by [USN:L4N4291N6 TEXT:"Alphabet"] (GOOGL.O) and [USN:L6N4470KC TEXT:"Intel"] (INTC.O) . Alibaba intends to use proceeds to fund AI development, including the expansion of related infrastructure. The share placement comes a week after Alibaba reported quarterly earnings in which it said it had already spent nearly half of its three-year capital expenditure plan. It brought forward its projected payback on AI investment to two and a half years from three due to surging demand for AI services. Its [USN:L4N44H0OB TEXT:"quarterly net profit"] fell 75% from a year earlier due primarily to AI-related spending. Last week, digital technology and AI division Alibaba Cloud launched its third data centre in South Korea , bringing its network to 104 availability zones across 30 regions. The move was a part of Alibaba's AI infrastructure pledge, announced in October, [USN:L5N3VU0SZ TEXT:"to invest 380 billion yuan"] ($56.54 billion) over three years.

item.title: Browns waive Dae'Quan Wright, paving reported return to college at LSU
item.description: The Cleveland Browns waived tight end Dae'Quan Wright on Sunday, paving a path for him to return to college football at LSU so long as he clears NFL waivers, his representation told ESPN.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Cleveland Browns waived tight end Dae'Quan Wright on Sunday, paving a path for him to return to college football at LSU so long as he clears NFL waivers, his representation told ESPN. Wright -- who signed with the Philadelphia Eagles as an undrafted free agent and then landed with Cleveland via waivers but hasn't appeared in either of their first two preseason games -- is believed to be the first player with an agreement in place to return to college football after signing an NFL contract as an undrafted free agent. Wright played the last two seasons for new LSU coach Lane Kiffin at Ole Miss, catching 39 passes for 635 yards and five touchdowns for the Rebels in 2025. He amassed 113 catches, 1,603 receiving yards and nine touchdown catches over four seasons at Virginia Tech (2022-23) and Ole Miss (2024-25). He's one of 16 football players who was granted a temporary restraining order earlier this week by a Louisiana judge to be deemed eligible for the 2026 college season. The NCAA initially ruled that all players whose eligibility expired after the 2025 season will not be eligible for its new five-year eligibility model. Wright officially entered the transfer portal Thursday and could join the 11th-ranked Tigers -- who open the season at home Sept. 5 vs. Clemson -- in the near future. The NCAA continues to fight against these players becoming eligible, receiving a stay from the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals on Friday. However, that stay doesn't erase the players who have already had their eligibility restored by TROs given by state-court judges across the country over the last few weeks. The other players who have reportedly entered the transfer portal this week after the Louisiana court ruling include one of Wright's Ole Miss teammates, defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, former SMU running back TJ Harden, former BYU offensive lineman Weylin Lapuaho, former James Madison linebacker Trent Hendrick, former Appalachian State defensive back Ethan Johnson and former New Mexico kicker Luke Drzewiecki. ESPN also reported this week that two other players in NFL camps, Jack Pyburn of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Wydett Williams Jr. of the Arizona Cardinals, can go back to school under the TRO. --Field Level Media

item.title: The Hormuz crude volume debate masks the real shortage of refined fuels
item.description: The crude oil market is currently engaged in the wrong debate over how much oil is actually moving via the Strait of Hormuz. It should be debating the constrained flows of refined products around Asia.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Russell
item.content:encoded: The crude oil market is currently engaged in the wrong debate over how much oil is actually moving via the Strait of Hormuz. It should be debating the constrained flows of refined products around Asia. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright has repeatedly claimed that much more crude is getting through the disputed strait than vessel-tracking analysts such as Kpler can see. One of Wright's claims was that about 15 million barrels per day (bpd) exited the Strait of Hormuz on a day last week, which if true would take volumes close to what they were before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. Wright has also said transits averaged about 9 million bpd over a seven-day period, although he didn't specify the exact dates and he has not provided details such as vessel names and their intended destinations. Vessel monitoring services estimate that around 5 million bpd is leaving the Strait of Hormuz, and that includes so-called dark transits and ship-to-ship transfers from smaller vessels to larger tankers in the Gulf of Oman. But the dispute over crude oil volumes is a false debate. If Wright is correct then Asia's oil imports will start to pick up in coming weeks as the crude he claims is leaving the Middle East arrives at ports. It's considerably easier to track import volumes, so it's merely a matter of time before the market can assess whether Wright is correct, or whether his numbers are overstated. In the meantime Asia's refined products markets remain stressed, as shown by sharply lower volumes and extremely elevated refining margins. Asia's imports of light and middle distillates for August are estimated by Kpler at 5.59 million bpd, in line with the 5.60 million bpd seen in July. However, these volumes are down 21% from the 7.08 million bpd average in the three months to the end of February. In effect, Asia is having to absorb a drop of 1.49 million bpd of key fuels such as diesel, jet fuel and gasoline. UNEVEN FALLOUT The impact is also not being evenly spread across the world's top-energy consuming continent, with less wealthy countries shouldering a bigger share of the loss of product volumes. Indonesia's imports of light and middle distillates are estimated at 432,000 bpd in August, the lowest in 13 months and down from an average of 533,000 bpd in the three months prior to the start of the Iran conflict. The Philippines is expected to see arrivals of 257,000 bpd of light and middle distillates in August, down from an average of 362,000 bpd in the three months to the end of February. A wealthier country like Australia, the world's biggest importer of diesel, is managing to secure the same levels of fuel, with August imports of light and middle distillates estimated by Kpler at 863,000 bpd, only slightly below the 880,000 bpd in the three months prior to the Iran war. But securing fuel is coming at a high cost, with product prices remaining near record high levels and refining margins staying elevated. The profit of making a barrel of gasoil, the building block for diesel, at a Singapore refinery was $71.29 a barrel on August 21, down from the record high of $85.63 on March 30 but also 226% higher than the $21.90 that prevailed on February 27, the day before the conflict started. Most of the stress in refined products has been felt in middle distillates, given the constrained supply of Middle East crudes, many of which are medium in gravity. Asia's refineries are tailored to process this type of oil into products such as diesel and jet fuel. But even gasoline, the main light distillate, is commanding a high premium, with the profit margin ending at $20.74 a barrel on August 21, up 159% from $8.00 on February 27. The message the market is giving is that while there may be sufficient crude oil reaching Asia, it's not necessarily the correct grades and those countries with spare refining capacity aren't ramping up exports to meet demand. item.title: Scandal-hit KPMG Australia to cut nearly 400 jobs, warns of difficult market
item.description: KPMG Australia, embroiled in scandal over the misuse of confidential client information, said on Monday it would cut about 5% of its workforce, affecting 27 partners and around 360 employees, and warned of difficult market conditions next year.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: KPMG Australia, embroiled in [USN:L1N42600F TEXT:"scandal"] over the misuse of confidential client information, said on Monday it would cut about 5% of its workforce, affecting 27 partners and around 360 employees, and warned of difficult market conditions next year. Most of the headcount reduction will take place in its consulting and business services divisions. KPMG Australia CEO John Sams said in a statement the firm recognised "challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue to do to rebuild trust." The firm also said it expected economic growth to remain subdued until at least 2028, weighing on client investment and extending decision-making timeframes. "While these conditions are likely to persist, we remain focused on what we can control," Sams said. KPMG has been under intense scrutiny from the Australian government and blue-chip clients since whistleblower allegations came to light in March that its staff used inside information to win lucrative audit contracts. The crisis triggered a [USN:L4N42V03T TEXT:"leadership overhaul"], with its former CEO, audit boss and chairman, as well as senior audit partners departing. Sams, previously a partner in the commercial advisory and transactions practice group, became chief executive last month. KPMG's total revenue slipped 1% to A$2.257 billion ($1.62 billion) in the year ended June 2026, as the loss of government contracts contributed to a 17% slump in consulting revenue. However, four of its five divisions posted revenue growth. Revenue rose 3% in the deal advisory and infrastructure division, 11% in both the tax and legal, and audit and assurance businesses, and 6.4% in the mid-market and private division. KPMG Australia has agreed not to [USN:L1N42N06L TEXT:"bid"] for any new federal government work until September 30, while reviews into the firm's governance, culture, ethics and integrity are underway, the government said in June. The firm also said it would simplify parts of its structure to create more integrated teams and align more closely with KPMG's global advisory services. ($1 = 1.3943 Australian dollars)

item.title: Shares flat in Asia before Iran sanctions news, Nvidia results
item.description: Share markets were flat in Asia on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran due later in the session, while the Canadian dollar dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Cole
item.content:encoded: Share markets were flat in Asia on Monday and oil prices eased as investors awaited details of threatened [USN:L1N44K02A TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] on Iran due later in the session, while the [USN:L6N44J03R TEXT:"Canadian dollar"] dipped as a trade war loomed with its southern neighbour. The entire tech sector is holding its breath for Nvidia's (NVDA.O) results on Wednesday; investors are aware how hard it will be for the chip maker to meet stratospheric expectations. Analysts are generally looking for quarterly revenue to almost double to around $92 billion, with full-year earnings guidance seen in a range of $103 billion to $105 billion. Market participants will also be hoping for some clarity on the outlook for U.S. interest rates when Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday, though his well-known aversion to forward guidance could lead to disappointment. "There are several reasons to expect to be underwhelmed," said Bruce Kasman, chief economist at JPMorgan, noting that past chairs have not wanted to front-run Fed decisions at the event. "Warsh will rather likely focus on aspects of his 'regime change' agenda," Kasman added. "As the Fed has already been moving toward shrinking the balance sheet, and the committee gave the balance sheet some attention in the July minutes, that might be the most likely topic for him to expound upon." Markets imply around a 40% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates when it meets on September 16 and are fully priced for a move by December. The odds could change depending on what U.S. inflation figures show this week, with median forecasts for core inflation expected to hold at 3.3% in July. Warsh is sure to face questions about Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's surprise announcement last week of at least a doubling in bond buybacks, aimed at restraining a rise in yields that was tightening financial conditions in the economy. His efforts have had little success so far, with 30-year yields back up at 5.2760% , not far from the recent 19-year peak of 5.3371%. Higher yields make debt more attractive compared to equities while lifting the discount applied to future earnings, highlighting the stretched nature of some valuations. SANCTIONS AND TRADE WARS Bessent is due to hold a news conference later on Monday to outline sanctions on Iran, which has shown no sign of relinquishing its control over the vital Strait of Hormuz. Brent slipped 1.0% to $93.43 ahead of the announcement, though that followed gains of 6.6% last week. U.S. crude eased 1.1% to $86.14 a barrel. Equity markets were quiet in early trade, with the Nikkei (.N225) near flat after having fallen almost 4% last week. South Korean shares (.KS11) eased 0.8%, while Taiwan (.TWII) dipped 0.5%. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) eased 0.2%. In Europe, EURO STOXX 50 futures , DAX futures and FTSE futures were all little changed. On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq futures were a fraction lower. In currency markets, the dollar added 0.1% against its Canadian counterpart to 1.3784 after Prime Minister Mark Carney said his country would respond to U.S. tariffs with levies of its own as trade talks broke down. Canada will impose tariffs on U.S. steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, along with some products that the U.S. previously targeted in Canada. The dollar was on the defensive elsewhere after having lost 0.8% last week against a basket of currencies at 96.832 . The euro held at $1.1675 after rising 0.9% last week, while the dollar was flat at 159.00 yen . The dollar has been undermined as investors fret that growing U.S. debt and policy uncertainties will erode the purchasing power of the currency, driving demand for scarcer assets including gold. The yellow metal firmed 0.4% to $4,623 an ounce , having climbed more than 14% for the month so far. If it holds this gain for all of August, it would be the biggest monthly rise on record.

item.title: Discussions Syrie-Israël de désescalade chapeautées par les USA
item.description: La Syrie et Israël ont pris part dimanche en Jordanie à des discussions à haut niveau chapeautées par les Etats-Unis destinées à apaiser les tensions entre les deux voisins à la suite des bombardements effectués par l'Etat hébreu en territoire syrien, a rapporté la presse officielle syrienne.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La Syrie et Israël ont pris part dimanche en Jordanie à des discussions à haut niveau chapeautées par les Etats-Unis destinées à apaiser les tensions entre les deux voisins à la suite des bombardements effectués par l'Etat hébreu en territoire syrien, a rapporté la presse officielle syrienne. Selon l'agence de presse syrienne Sana, citant une source diplomatique et le ministère des affaires étrangères à Damas, ces discussions se sont focalisées sur des dispositifs concrets pour stopper les frappes, les opérations et les arrestations effectuées par Israël. Il a également été question de relancer les négociations vers un accord sécuritaire entre les deux pays, lequel pourrait ultérieurement servir de base à un accord élargi, a-t-on déclaré de même source. Par ailleurs, les deux camps ont évoqué des moyens d'apaiser les [USN:L8N44H0PX TEXT:"tensions"] entre Israël et la Turquie, et d'éviter que cette rivalité ait des répercussions sur le territoire syrien. Le ministre syrien des Affaires étrangères avait déclaré samedi à Reuters que Damas s'attendait à ce que les négociations sécuritaires avec Israël reprennent bientôt. Asaad al-Shaibani avait toutefois ajouté qu'il y avait un manque de confiance entre les deux parties. Ces négociations sécuritaires ont été suspendues au début de la guerre en Iran, provoquée en février dernier par la campagne de bombardements lancée par les Etats-Unis et Israël. Puis, selon le chef de la diplomatie syrienne, Damas a rompu tout contact avec Israël à la suite des [USN:L8N44F0JE TEXT:"bombardements"] effectués contre la base aérienne d'Abou Douhour la semaine dernière. Washington cherche depuis plus d'un an à chapeauter un accord sécuritaire entre Israël et le gouvernement du président syrien Ahmed al-Charaa, ancien commandant des rebelles ayant provoqué la chute de Bachar al-Assad en décembre 2024. DOUTES D'après Asaad al-Shaibani, les deux camps étaient convenus de "presque tout" sur le papier en début d'année, notamment de la mise en place de zones de sécurité dans le sud de la Syrie et d'une zone 'tampon' où seules des troupes de l'Onu seraient autorisées. Mais, a-t-il dit, Damas a douté de la volonté réelle d'Israël de mettre en oeuvre cet accord. Aucun commentaire n'a été obtenu auprès des services du Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu. Lors de la réunion organisée dimanche, a rapporté l'agence Sana, les représentants syriens ont indiqué que Damas avait toujours pour priorités immédiates le retrait de l'armée israélienne des positions contrôlées avant la chute de Bachar al-Assad ainsi que le plein respect de l'accord de 1974. Damas a aussi souligné auprès des émissaires israéliens qu'il n'accepterait aucun accord limitant son droit à rebâtir et développer son armée ou déterminant ses alliances et partenariats, a écrit la Sana. Israël a effectué des incursions supplémentaires en Syrie et saisi des territoires stratégiques, notamment la partie syrienne du Mont Hermon qui surplombe la capitale Damas, à la suite de la chute de Bachar al-Assad. L'Etat hébreu, qui effectue de longue date des frappes aériennes en Syrie contre ce qu'il présente comme des cibles militaires iraniennes et des milices alignées sur Téhéran dont le Hezbollah libanais, a procédé à une nouvelle campagne de bombardements et a dit également mener des "missions de protection" de la minorité druze dans le sud-ouest du pays. Damas nie représenter une menace pour Israël et réclame la fin des bombardements et incursions de Tsahal. Syrie et Israël sont techniquement en guerre depuis 1948. L'Etat hébreu s'est emparé du Plateau du Golan lors de la guerre des Six-Jours en 1967 avant de l'annexer en 1981 - cette annexion a été reconnue par les Etats-Unis mais rejetée par une grande partie de la communauté internationale.

item.title: Burnham se rend en Ukraine, veut aider Kyiv à produire des missiles longue-portée
item.description: Le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham effectue lundi un déplacement en Ukraine, sa première visite à l'étranger depuis son entrée en fonction, lors duquel il va annoncer la volonté de Londres de soutenir Kyiv dans le renforcement de sa production locale de missile à longue portée.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Macaskill
item.content:encoded: Le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham effectue lundi un déplacement en Ukraine, sa première visite à l'étranger depuis son entrée en fonction, lors duquel il va annoncer la volonté de Londres de soutenir Kyiv dans le renforcement de sa production locale de missile à longue portée. A l'occasion de cette visite, Andy Burnham va co-présider une réunion de la "coalition des volontaires" et s'entretenir avec le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky. Le dirigeant britannique va annoncer que la Grande-Bretagne a autorisé le fabricant européen de missiles MBDA à divulguer des informations classifiées sur les composants de fabrication britannique utilisés pour la production du missile de croisière à longue portée SCALP, a fait savoir Downing Street. Cela permettra à la France et à l'Ukraine de mettre en place des chaînes d'assemblage locales pour ce missile, qui repose sur une technologie conjointe franco-britannique, ont ajouté les services d'Andy Burnham. "La sécurité de l'Ukraine est notre sécurité", a dit le Premier ministre britannique dans un communiqué, soulignant que Londres se tiendrait au côté de Kyiv "aussi longtemps qu'il le faudra". Parmi les principaux soutiens de l'Ukraine à la suite de l'invasion menée par la Russie en février 2022, la Grande-Bretagne a été le premier pays à annoncer son intention de fournir à Kyiv des chars d'assaut et des missiles de croisière de fabrication occidentale. Moscou a mis en garde Londres la semaine dernière contre les "conséquences" de la livraison de drones à Kyiv, accusant la Grande-Bretagne d'accroître son rôle dans le conflit. Il est attendu qu'Andy Burnham utilise cette visite en Ukraine pour réaffirmer la volonté de Londres à continuer de mener des efforts pour renforcer la sécurité de l'Ukraine. Volodimir Zelensky avait été le mois dernier le premier dirigeant étranger reçu par Andy Burnham depuis sa prise de fonction à Downing Street.

item.title: Drone attack kills two children, burns logistics hub in Russia's Krasnodar
item.description: Two children were killed and another nine people, including seven children, were injured after drone debris hit a private childcare centre in Krasnodar, southern Russia, overnight, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two children were killed and another nine people, including seven children, were injured after drone debris hit a private childcare centre in Krasnodar, southern Russia, overnight, Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. In Ukraine, a Russian attack on the outskirts of the northeastern city of Kharkiv killed three people, the governor [USN:L1N44K052 TEXT:"said"] on Telegram late on Sunday. Ukraine is [USN:S8N3Y606D TEXT:"seeking"] additional interceptor missiles from the U.S. and Europe, its key allies, to repel such attacks, in its fifth year of war with Russia. Debris fell on apartment buildings and warehouses caught fire in Krasnodar, Kondratyev said on the Telegram messaging app. The attack caused a fire at a logistics hub of Russian online retailer Ozon, the company said on Telegram. In Russia's Nevinnomysk, a chemical production area in the Stavropol region next to Krasnodar, a drone attack on an industrial area was repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov [USN:P8N44101E TEXT:"said"] on Telegram early on Monday. Ukraine has stepped up attacks on logistics hubs and warehouses across Russia, bringing the war which Russia started in February 2022 closer to ordinary Russians, some of whom make their living from selling goods online. In comments published on Saturday, Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L6N44J044 TEXT:"said"] that Kyiv had opened a "Pandora's box" with its strikes on Russian economic targets and that Moscow would hit back at Ukraine's "most sensitive economic sectors".

item.title: Samsung Electronics shares skid as record shareholder returns disappoint
item.description: Shares of Samsung Electronics fell 8% in early trade on Monday after the company’s record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of Samsung’s AI-fueled cash windfalls and greater clarity on share buybacks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) fell 8% in early trade on Monday after the company’s record $79 billion shareholder-return plan disappointed investors who had expected a larger share of Samsung’s AI-fueled cash windfalls and greater clarity on share buybacks. The South Korean chipmaker said on Friday this year's shareholder returns would be from 90 trillion won to 110 trillion won ($65 billion to $80 billion), including 30 trillion won in cash dividends in the third quarter. While five times the previous record-high returns of 2020, analysts said the projected returns were smaller than they had anticipated and that they had expected more details on the buyback plans. Samsung said it continues to commit 50% of free cash flow accumulated over the three-year period to shareholders, under its 2024 to 2026 shareholder return policy. Rival SK Hynix (000660.KS) said last week it will buy back and cancel 40 trillion won of treasury shares and allocate more than 50% of its free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027 to boost shareholder returns. SK Hynix was up 0.4%. The benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) index fell 1.5%. "Unlike SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics did not mention the possibility of raising its existing shareholder return policy, nor did it announce a plan to cancel treasury shares that could more directly contribute to the stock price increase, which is disappointing," Sohn In-joon, an analyst at Eugene Securities, said in a report. "Big capital returns, slightly below expectations," Morgan Stanley said in a report. It said investors would need to watch Samsung’s January decision on the allocation of the remaining 60 trillion won to 80 trillion won, as well as the company’s next capital-return framework, which will take effect next year. ($1 = 1,383.7100 won)

item.title: Ikitau eyes return to crowded Wallabies midfield for Argentina challenge
item.description: Len Ikitau is ready to return to the Wallabies' midfield against Argentina after injury troubles and has an open mind about where he should fit in new coach Les Kiss's plans.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Len Ikitau is ready to return to the Wallabies' midfield against Argentina after injury troubles and has an open mind about where he should fit in new coach Les Kiss's plans. Ikitau missed Kiss's first tests in charge against Japan while sidelined with an ankle problem but will be expected to slot back into the starting 15 for the first Pumas match in San Salvador on Saturday. Quite where the classy centre starts is up in the air, given he is capable in both positions. Hunter Paisami also had strong outings in the wins over Japan in the number 12 jersey that Ikitau wore under former coach Joe Schmidt in a midfield pairing with Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii. Ikitau said the midfield competition could only be good for the Wallabies and he would be happy to take a bench spot if Kiss so desired. “Obviously I’ve only played 12 since Joseph’s come in, and I’ve only played 13 for the Brumbies, but for me, I love playing 12 or 13,” Ikitau said. “We’ll get to that when we get there, but happy to do my part whether that’s 12 or 13. Or 23 or 22. I’m quite happy as just a centre ... being able to cover both.” Queensland Reds centre Isaac Henry is another midfield option for Kiss, and impressed Ikitau as the starting outside centre in the big win over Japan in Townsville while Suaalii was nursing a hamstring strain. “It was pretty cool, especially seeing Zaccy (Henry) debut and watching Hunter play again. I thought they did an amazing job in terms of leading the back line." Argentina will be a step up in class for the Wallabies despite their slow start in the July tests, losing to England and Scotland at home in the Nations Championship. Australia have had mixed fortunes in the last two-test tours of Argentina in 2022 and 2024, winning the openers before getting thrashed in the second matches. “So for us, we want to be consistent in the way we play and just make sure that we’re putting in good performances and performances that we’re proud of," said Ikitau.

item.title: ExxonMobil temporarily halts operations at Guyana site after fire, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: U.S. oil major ExxonMobil suspended operations at a facility off the coast of Guyana after a laundry-room fire broke out on a floating vessel, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing a company statement.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. oil major ExxonMobil (XOM.N) suspended operations at a facility off the coast of Guyana after a laundry-room fire broke out on a floating vessel, Bloomberg News reported on Sunday, citing a company statement. According to the report, the fire on the Liza Unity floating production, storage and offloading vessel was quickly extinguished, but crude offloading was affected by the temporary halt. ExxonMobil did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. Operations were suspended as part of the company's established safety response and will resume following completion of the necessary checks, the report said. All staff aboard the ship were safe and accounted for, it added. According to recent government data, the Exxon Mobil consortium's oil output in Guyana [USN:S0N43903A TEXT:"reached 895,000 barrels per day"] in May and 869,000 bpd in June.

item.title: Browns coach: Deshaun Watson's comments won't affect QB decision
item.description: Deshaun Watson's criticisms of Cleveland Browns fans won't be part of the decision on whether Watson or Shedeur Sanders will be named Monday as the team's starting quarterback.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deshaun Watson's criticisms of Cleveland Browns fans won't be part of the decision on whether Watson or Shedeur Sanders will be named Monday as the team's starting quarterback. Browns first-year coach Todd Monken said the piercing comments are a non-factor as he determines which player is the best option to be the club's QB1. "He emptied his heart a little bit, and I don't think that says who he is," Monken told reporters Sunday, one day after a 31-7 home loss to the Buffalo Bills. "I see the competitor in him. I see the everyday work he puts in, and he wants to be back. "He wants to get back to where he was as best he can, and that's hard. And again, I think the moment just got him after the game, and it can get all of us." Watson alluded to his belief that he would be facing "17 away games" if he were named the starter. Cleveland fans vociferously showered Watson with boos during Saturday's contest, his first at home since tearing his right Achilles tendon during Week 7 of the 2024 season. When Watson suffered the injury, the fans applauded, and he hasn't forgotten that. Watson later injured the Achilles again and underwent a second surgery. He didn't appear in a game in 2025. "The whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said Saturday. "It's a little bit (more) personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing. So, yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And, yeah, just move on. "Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. And that same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt. So, what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer?" Cleveland has been outscored 65-17 in its first two preseason games. Watson started the first one and guided the team to 10 first-half points in a loss to the Chicago Bears. Sanders started against the Bills and led the team to a first-quarter touchdown. Watson has completed 59.3 percent of his passes for 162 yards and one interception this preseason. Sanders has connected on 68.2 percent of his passes for 153 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Watson and Sanders have been splitting first-team repetitions in training camp practices. "Even with (Saturday), we have to take in the full body of work," Monken said. "That's one opportunity that they had on the field, both of them, just like the week before, an opportunity. Just like the practices against the Bills were an opportunity to showcase their ability and others' ability and where they're at this point, where we're at as an offense. "I look at it (as): What has been the full body of work? And then, ultimately, who gives us the best chance to win Week 1? "I'm not going to let one half of football, one frustrating moment, dictate what our decision is going to be that we think is in the best interest of the Browns moving forward and especially Week 1." Watson, who turns 31 next month, was traded from the Houston Texans to the Browns prior to the 2022 season. Cleveland subsequently gave him a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract. In addition to the Achilles injury, he also had his career derailed by an 11-game suspension in 2022 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy after the league's investigation into sexual misconduct allegations involving more than two dozen massage therapists. In 19 games with Cleveland, Watson has a 9-10 record and has thrown 19 touchdowns to 12 interceptions. Earlier in his career, Watson was a Pro Bowl selection three straight seasons (2018-20) for the Texans. He passed for career highs of 4,823 yards and 33 touchdowns in 2020. Sanders, 24, was a fifth-round draft pick last season and went 3-4 as a starter while playing eight games. He passed for 1,400 yards and seven touchdowns against 10 interceptions and was named to the Pro Bowl Games as a replacement after other quarterbacks withdrew. --Field Level Media

item.title: Offices, schools closed in southern Taiwan due to torrential rain
item.description: Torrential rains across southern Taiwan forced offices and schools to close on Monday and some rail services were disrupted, with officials bracing for a typhoon to hit the north of the island later in the week.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Torrential rains across southern Taiwan forced offices and schools to close on Monday and some rail services were disrupted, with officials bracing for a typhoon to hit the north of the island later in the week. A low-pressure system has hovered over southern Taiwan for the past few days, bringing heavy rain and causing flooding. The local governments of the two cities of Kaohsiung and Tainan, home to more than four million people, ordered offices and schools closed, as did the counties of Pingtung and Chiayi and the mountainous eastern counties of Taitung and Hualien. The Kaohsiung government said it expected cumulative rainfall over the five-day period of the low-pressure system to exceed 1.3 metres (4.3 feet), nearly half what the city typically expects in an entire year. Taiwan Railway said there would be disruptions on the main east coast line and trains to and from Kaohsiung and Taitung with express services cancelled and local trains dependent on weather conditions. "If you've got nothing on, for goodness sake don't go out," Taitung county chief April Yao wrote on her Facebook page. Taiwan's Central Weather Administration said separately that Typhoon Saudel, currently heading towards Japan's southern Okinawa region, is expected to pass by the northern part of Taiwan early on Friday before reaching the eastern coast of China.

item.title: Diamondbacks rally in 7th, top Reds to keep pace in wild-card race
item.description: Ildemaro Vargas hit a go-ahead two-run triple in a four-run seventh inning, Corbin Carroll had two extra-base hits and an RBI, and the host Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a three-run deficit for a 5-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday in Phoenix.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ildemaro Vargas hit a go-ahead two-run triple in a four-run seventh inning, Corbin Carroll had two extra-base hits and an RBI, and the host Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a three-run deficit for a 5-3 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Sunday in Phoenix. Vargas and Tim Tawa had two hits apiece, and six relievers combined to throw six scoreless innings in the D-backs' 39th comeback victory. They have won three of their last four. Tawa singled to lead off the seventh against Andrew Abbott (6-9). Jordan Lawlar also singled, and James McCann drew a four-pitch walk to knock out Abbott, who had given up one run in six innings. Pinch hitter Lars Nootbaar hit a slow groundout to pitcher Luis Mey that brought in Tawa, and Vargas followed with a hard grounder past second base against a drawn-in infield that rolled to the wall in right-center to drive in two. Carroll's sacrifice fly scored Vargas to make it 5-3. Sal Stewart and Dane Myers had two hits each for the Reds, who have lost four of their last six. Kevin Ginkel entered with two outs and a runner on first in the ninth and pitched around a fielding error by Vargas to get Tyler Stephenson looking for his second save of the season. Jonathan Loiaisiga (5-3), the third Arizona reliever, pitched a scoreless seventh for the win. Stewart increased his major league-leading RBI total to 98 with a run-scoring single in a three-run third off Arizona starter Mitch Bratt. Eugenio Suarez capped the rally with a two-run single for a 3-0 lead. Elly De La Cruz doubled to open the inning and scored on Stewart's opposite-field hit to right. Dane Myers doubled to right before Suarez's single. Abbott gave up seven hits and four runs in six-plus innings. He had six strikeouts and two walks. The D-backs (69-62) kept pace with the Philadelphia Phillies (73-58) and San Diego Padres (71-62) in the race for the final two National League wild-card spots. All three clubs won Sunday. Bratt gave up five hits and three runs in three innings, with three walks and three strikeouts. Carroll tripled off the center-field fence with one out in the sixth and scored on Gabriel Moreno's sacrifice fly to make it 3-1. Carroll has 16 triples. No other major leaguer has more than seven. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shein saldrá a bolsa con un valor de hasta 27.000 millones de dólares en Hong Kong
item.description: La empresa de moda rápida por internet Shein apunta a una valoración de hasta 27.000 millones de dólares con su oferta pública inicial de 13.860 millones de dólares hongkoneses (1.770 millones de dólares), que se lanzó este lunes en Hong Kong, según la documentación presentada por la compañía.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La empresa de moda rápida por internet Shein apunta a una valoración de hasta 27.000 millones de dólares con su oferta pública inicial de 13.860 millones de dólares hongkoneses (1.770 millones de dólares), que se lanzó este lunes en Hong Kong, según la documentación presentada por la compañía. Shein va a vender 280 millones de acciones a un precio que oscilará entre los 47,60 y los 49,50 dólares de Hong Kong por acción, según los documentos. La empresa anunciará el precio definitivo el 31 de agosto y comenzará a cotizar el 1 de septiembre. Shein alcanzará una valoración cercana a los 27.000 millones de dólares en el extremo superior del rango de precios, lo que supone un importante descenso respecto de rondas anteriores de financiación privada, que tasaron al comerciante por internet en 98.200 millones de dólares en 2022, y 64.000 millones de dólares en 2023 y abril de 2024. Los inversionistas principales, liderados por Boyu, Tiger Global y General Atlantic, han suscrito acciones de Shein por un valor aproximado de 383 millones de dólares, según el folleto de emisión. Tencent (0700.HK) , Greenwoods, Taikang Life y UBS Asset Management también comprarán acciones. La salida a bolsa se da en un escenario en que la desaceleración del crecimiento de los ingresos y el debilitamiento de las ganancias brutas lastran el negocio de Shein, y además hay preocupación por el aumento de los costos, un mayor escrutinio y una competencia cada vez más intensa. Shein, conocida por vender vestidos a 5 dólares y pantalones a 10 dólares a compradores de unos 160 países, tuvo pérdidas trimestrales de 99 millones de dólares tras la supresión en Estados Unidos de una exención de aranceles a las importaciones de paquetes pequeños. La salida a bolsa de Shein es la mayor emisión de nuevas acciones en Hong Kong en 2026 y la tercera mayor salida a bolsa de Asia, por detrás de CXMT (688825.SS) y China Resources New Energy (001248.SZ) , que recaudaron 9.800 millones y 3.600 millones de dólares en china continental. (1 dólar = 7,8400 dólares de Hong Kong)

item.title: California expected to seek TV channel sales from Paramount-Warner, WSJ reports
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is expected to ask Paramount to divest some cable channels and commit to keeping its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. before he signs off on their merger, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is expected to ask Paramount (PSKY.O) to divest some cable channels and commit to keeping its movie studio separate from Warner Bros. (WBD.O) before he signs off on their merger, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Paramount and California state officials are [USN:L6N44J066 TEXT:"set to meet"] on Monday to discuss potential ways to settle the state's antitrust lawsuit, the report said. Lawyers from both sides met on Friday to lay out an agenda for Monday's meeting, including discussions about the cable and motion-picture businesses, the Journal reported. Paramount, Warner Bros. Discovery, and the California Attorney General's office did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. Last month, California and 11 states[USN:L6N43G09L TEXT:" sued to block"] Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros., alleging the deal would lessen competition in film distribution and cable television, harming theaters and pay TV distributors. Some states argued the deal would harm theaters and television distributors, raise prices for consumers and make wages less competitive for workers. Paramount has said the deal will allow it to produce more, not less, and CEO David Ellison has vowed the combined film studios would release 30 movies a year. The states have called that commitment unenforceable.

item.title: Cubs run it up on Mariners, end losing streak with 19-2 win
item.description: Ian Happ and Pedro Ramirez hit grand slams as the Chicago Cubs defeated the host Seattle Mariners 19-2 Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ian Happ and Pedro Ramirez hit grand slams as the Chicago Cubs defeated the host Seattle Mariners 19-2 Sunday afternoon. Pete Crow-Armstrong and Michael Conforto also homered and right-hander Aaron Civale (6-7) pitched four innings of scoreless relief as the Cubs snapped a three-game losing streak. Chicago brought home nine runs in the eighth inning and tallied 17 hits in the beatdown. Randy Arozarena homered for Seattle, which had won five of its previous seven games. That gave Arozarena a sixth consecutive season with at least 20 homers and 20 steals, an accomplishment matched only by Barry Bonds (nine straight), Bobby Bonds (seven), Bobby Abreu (seven) and Willie Mays (six) in MLB history. Arozarena, who hit leadoff and walk-off homers Saturday, went deep again in the first inning Sunday to left field off Cubs starter Shota Imanaga. He became the second player to ever hit consecutive leadoff homers with a walk-off in between, duplicating Crow-Armstrong's feat from earlier in the week. The Mariners made it 2-0 in the second as Victor Robles drew a one-out walk, stole second and third and scored on catcher Carson Kelly's throwing error. Conforto led off the third with a homer to right off Mariners starter Bryce Miller (4-8). With two outs, Miller issued three straight walks before Happ's slam off the right field foul pole made it 5-2 Chicago. The Cubs extended their lead to 6-2 in the fifth after Miller walked the bases full with no outs. Bregman grounded into a forceout to score the run before reliever Jose A. Ferrer got out of the jam with a double play. Chicago scored again in the sixth after Ramirez and pinch hitter Tyrone Taylor led off with singles. After a double play moved Ramirez to third, Crow-Armstrong reached on an infield single that made it 7-2. In the eighth, Crow-Armstrong blasted a two-run shot off reliever Michael Rucker and Ramirez hit his slam, a liner just over the left field wall, off Mariners backup catcher Jhonny Pereda. Seattle third baseman Weston Wilson took the mound in the ninth and allowed the final three runs. Kelly eschewed his catching gear to pitch a scoreless ninth for the Cubs. Miller allowed just two hits (the two homers) over 4 1/3 innings but was charged with six runs. The right-hander walked seven and struck out five. Imanaga lasted two-plus innings and gave up two runs (one earned) on five hits over 72 pitches. The lefty walked two and fanned four. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil falls ahead of US announcement on new Iran sanctions
item.description: Brent crude futures fell to $93.45.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: Oil prices slipped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors took profits ahead of an expected announcement from Washington about imposing more sanctions on Iran that may further disrupt supplies from the Middle East. Brent crude futures fell $1.22, or 1.29%, to $93.17 by 0035 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $85.86 a barrel, down $1.20, or 1.38%. Both contracts posted their second weekly gains last week, up more than 5%, as peace talks between the U.S. and Iran hit a stalemate, capping oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz where a fifth of the world's supply used to transit. U.S. Treasury Secretary [USN:L1N44K02A TEXT:"Scott Bessent"], set to hold a press conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners. "It is unclear whether U.S. policy to economically isolate Iran will prove effective," Vivek Dhar, a commodities analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, wrote in a note. "But if the U.S. measures do work as intended, Iran's ability to respond via increased violence becomes a growing risk for energy markets to consider." Iran has condemned U.S. plans to announce new sanctions even as President Masoud Pezeshkian called for a [USN:L6N44J01G TEXT:"diplomatic solution"]. "The more pragmatic members of the Iranian leadership would prefer to de-escalate but the hardliners would probably prefer to fight to the bitter end," IG markets analyst Tony Sycamore said. "I think by the end of this week we will have a good idea which side of the Iranian leadership has the upper hand." Offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers [USN:L1N44I07T TEXT:"have declined"] and prices have jumped as the U.S. blockade has cut Tehran's shipments, according to trade sources. However, Iran has granted permission for a number of [USN:L1N44J01S TEXT:"Iraqi oil tankers"] to pass through the Strait following repeated requests from Baghdad, Iran’s state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.
