In its announcement for the $10.2 billion share placement, Alibaba did not reveal additional details on its investment plans by category of its planned AI-related investment. It did not comment beyond its regulatory disclosure. Last week, Alibaba reported its results for the April-to-June quarter, saying it had already spent nearly half of its three-year capex investment plan. It said its expected payback on AI-related investments was on track to fall to 2.5 years from 3 years, driven by surging demand. Alibaba's net profit for the quarter [USN:L4N44H0OB TEXT:"fell 75%"] from a year earlier as it ramped up its AI-related capital expenditures. "In order to be able to capture that future growth, we first need to make these capex investments to build out the necessary compute capacity," CEO Eddie Wu said on an earnings call. The company's share offering has been met with strong demand from investors, including sovereign wealth funds, two people familiar with the deal told Reuters. They could not be named because the information was not public. Alibaba increased the size of the offering after the deal was oversubscribed, the people familiar with the matter said. Morgan Stanley, HSBC, UBS and CICC are serving as joint bookrunners of the Alibaba offering, said one of the sources and a third person with knowledge of the matter. The banks did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The share placement was not registered under U.S. securities laws as an offshore transaction, meaning American investors were not eligible to participate, Alibaba said. Since 2022, the global AI boom has fuelled staggering capital outlays on infrastructure and data centers, including in the U.S. and China. The four major U.S. hyperscalers - Microsoft (MSFT.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Meta (META.O) - together are expected to spend roughly $725 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, much of it tied to AI data centers, chips and cloud infrastructure. ($1 = 7.8396 Hong Kong dollars)

item.title: From science fair to strategic showcase: a decade of China’s robot games
item.description: Unlike the human Olympics, Team China is collecting almost all the medals.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: It’s been called the Robot Olympics. But unlike the human Olympics, Team China is collecting almost all the medals. Over the past decade, robotic competitions in China have provided a window into the advances of a now-surging sector – and the importance of its success as a strategic industry singled out by President Xi Jinping. Once a curiosity organized by academic teams and hobbyists, China’s robot games have become a national showcase celebrated by state media — and, increasingly, a proving ground for commercial products from companies looking to show real-world applications beyond the spectacle. The five-day World Humanoid Robot Games – the latest and biggest incarnation of the competition – began on Saturday in Beijing. Here’s a timeline of how the competitions, and the underlying technology, have developed: 1999 - 2014: Robotics as college sport Robotics competitions in China started as lower-budget affairs backed by an industry association and the local government of Fujian. The competitors were mostly college teams. The vibe was more science project than showcase for the high-flying companies that emerged later. In one showcase event, small, wheeled robots played a competitive version of soccer with a limited range of pre-programmed automation to avoid collisions and find the ball. 2015: Robotics as the “crown jewel” In 2015, Beijing hosted the first World Robot Conference, marking the industry’s emergence as a national priority. A year earlier, Xi had declared robotics was the “crown jewel” of advanced manufacturing, according to state media. At the 2015 exhibition, mobile robots faced off in badminton demonstrations, tracking shuttlecocks and returning volleys. It was a crowd-pleasing showcase — but hardly a breakthrough. Robots like this relied on distance-image sensors developed in the 2010s and an even-older technology for estimating the track of an object pioneered by British defence researchers in the 1990s. 2023: From the lab to the living room By 2023, the World Robot Conference had become a high-profile venue for established companies to showcase innovation and build buzz. Along the way attention began to shift to China's competitive advantage on pricing. Xiaomi's robot dog "Cyberdog" drew a ring of onlookers filming on smartphones. The Cyberdog, first released as a hobbyist platform, cost about $1,500 on release. By comparison, Boston Dynamics’ quadruped Spot was selling for over $75,000. 2025-2026: From stumbling start to great leap In April 2025, humanoid robots lined up alongside human runners for the world's first robot half-marathon in Beijing. Engineers jogged alongside their machines, ready to intervene. Only a fraction of the robots that started the course finished. Some collapsed on the starting line. Others crashed into the railing just a few metres in. A year later, the robots were ready. A Unitree H1 robot sprinted unaccompanied down the finishing straight of the second Beijing half-marathon — no chaperone in sight. Of the more than 100 robot teams that entered the competition in 2026, 47 finished, state media reported. Most striking: a humanoid robot by Chinese smartphone maker Honor named “Flash” ran the half marathon autonomously in 50 minutes and 26 seconds. That was faster than the human world record set just a month earlier by almost 7 minutes. Analysts and executives attributed the sharp and widespread improvements to the competitiveness of a growing supply chain bolstered by subsidies and the falling cost of components. The visible hand of the state drove some of those gains. Beijing's 2021 five-year blueprint for the robotics sector had promised subsidies, research tax breaks and financing, setting a goal for China to become “a global wellspring of robotics technology innovation.” 2026 and onward: It’s all in the hands In 2026, the World Humanoid Robot Games add a challenge for robotic hands. Robots will be judged on their speed and accuracy in precision tasks: tightening screws, opening bottles and picking up beads with tweezers. Analysts say engineering a hand is the most complex challenge for building a humanoid that can work with the precision and touch of a human. The shift to work tasks in the games also reflects the increasingly crowded industry’s biggest problem: showing prototypes can work in the real world.

item.content:encoded: Shein pourrait atteindre une valorisation de $27 mds lors de son IPO à Hong Kong HONG KONG, 24 août (Reuters) - La valorisation de Shein a chuté d'environ 70% par rapport au pic de près de 100 milliards de dollars atteint lors d'un tour de table effectué il y a quatre ans, alors que le géant en ligne chinois de la mode éphémère entend lever jusqu'à 1,77 milliards de dollars en vue de son introduction en Bourse à Hong Kong. Paris et Berlin appellent à la libération de la militante hongkongaise Chow Hang-tung La France et l'Allemagne ont appelé vendredi à la libération immédiate de Chow Hang-tung, militante des droits de l'Homme reconnue coupable par la Haute Cour de Hong Kong d'incitation à la subversion avec un autre activiste, Lee Cheuk-yan. Macron recevra le prince héritier saoudien les 23-24 août Le président français Emmanuel Macron recevra le prince héritier d'Arabie saoudite Mohammed ben Salmane les 23 et 24 août, une rencontre lors de laquelle ils devraient aborder les tensions actuelles au Moyen-Orient, a déclaré jeudi l'Elysée. Cisjordanie: Paris, Berlin, Rome et Londres condamnent le projet de colonie israélien E1 Les dirigeants français, allemand, italien et britannique considèrent comme "inacceptable" et "préoccupante" la décision d'Israël de publier des appels d'offres liés à un projet de colonie dit E1 en Cisjordanie, qui "porte atteinte à la continuité territoriale des territoires palestiniens". Israël met en garde la Turquie contre toute "aventure dangereuse" en Syrie Le ministre israélien de la Défense, Israel Katz, a déclaré jeudi que le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan entraînait la Turquie dans "des aventures dangereuses en Syrie", et qu'Israël ne permettrait à aucune entité de menacer sa propre sécurité. La France "condamne" les sanctions prises par les Etrats-Unis contre la CPI La France a condamné mercredi les sanctions annoncées la veille par les Etats-Unis à l'encontre de la présidente et d'un haut procureur de la Cour pénale internationale (CPI), citant une "atteinte" envers la juridiction et l'ensemble de ses parties prenantes.

item.title: Shein's pursuit of an IPO: From New York to London to Hong Kong
item.description: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein launched its long-awaited Hong Kong IPO on Monday, aiming to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) at a valuation of close to $27 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein [USN:L1N44K04U TEXT:"launched its long-awaited Hong Kong IPO"] on Monday, aiming to raise up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) at a valuation of close to $27 billion. It will price the offering on August 28 and debut on September 1, according to the offering prospectus. Here's a timeline of the Singapore-headquartered company's prolonged attempts to list: JANUARY 2022 Shein revives New York listing plans. Founder Chris Xu considers changing his citizenship to bypass tougher rules for offshore IPOs in China, Reuters reports. It had first explored a U.S. IPO two years earlier but shelved it amid volatile markets and U.S.-China tensions. FEBRUARY 2022 Shein pauses U.S. listing plans due to volatile capital markets amid Russia's invasion of Ukraine, sources say. MARCH 2023 Shein seeks to raise about $2 billion in new funding, eyeing a U.S. listing in the second half of 2023. MAY 2023 Two dozen bipartisan U.S. lawmakers urge the Securities and Exchange Commission to halt Shein's IPO pending forced-labour verification, Reuters reports. JUNE/JULY 2023 Shein makes moves to register with U.S. regulators and talks to NYSE, Nasdaq and at least three banks about a New York listing, Reuters reports. NOVEMBER 2023 Shein targets a $90 billion valuation, Bloomberg News reports. The company confidentially files for a U.S. IPO and lawmakers renew demands for forced-labour proof tied to its cheap clothing. DECEMBER 2023 Shein opens [USN:L4N3D623N TEXT:"talks"] with the London Stock Exchange about a possible listing in the United Kingdom, Sky News reports. JANUARY 2024 Shein seeks Beijing's approval for a U.S. listing to meet new rules for Chinese firms going public abroad, Reuters reports. FEBRUARY 2024 Republican Senator Marco Rubio asks the SEC to block a New York listing unless the company makes additional disclosures about its business operations and "the serious risks of doing business" in China. The UK's then-finance minister Jeremy Hunt meets Shein's chairman as London courts the listing, Reuters reports. MAY 2024 Shein [USN:L1N3HF0HY TEXT:"steps up preparations"] for a London listing after regulatory hurdles and pushback from U.S. lawmakers for its New York float. Senior British lawmakers also question its suitability and demand scrutiny. JUNE 2024 Shein meets the UK's Labour Party and [USN:L1N3IM0DM TEXT:"confidentially"] files with Britain's markets regulator. A human rights [USN:L4N3IO16R TEXT:"group"] and, in July, a [USN:L1N3J90VP TEXT:"campaign"] backed by British retail consultant and television personality Mary Portas, push to block the London float. OCTOBER 2024 Shein holds [USN:L4N3LF0DV TEXT:"informal"] investor meetings for the planned London IPO. DECEMBER 2024 Britain's [USN:L8N3NA0OJ TEXT:"financial regulator"] delays approval to vet supply chains and legal risks; Shein [USN:L8N3NE11D TEXT:"weighs"] asking for a waiver on rules requiring 10% of shares sold to the public. JANUARY 2025 Shein targets a London listing in the [USN:L8N3O40VR TEXT:"first half"], but tells UK [USN:L2N3OK0EE TEXT:"lawmakers"] it bars Chinese cotton in U.S.-sold goods after a senior lawmaker [USN:L8N3O61M9 TEXT:"flags"] concerns to regulators. FEBRUARY 2025 Shein is set to [USN:L8N3OX1M6 TEXT:"cut its valuation"] in a potential London IPO to around $50 billion, nearly a quarter less than its 2023 fundraising value. The Financial Times reports the listing may [USN:L4N3P50GV TEXT:"slip"] into the second half after U.S. President Donald Trump scraps the "de minimis" customs duty exemption on low-value ecommerce parcels. Shein is under pressure to [USN:L3N3P80IH TEXT:"cut its valuation"] to about $30 billion, Bloomberg News reports. APRIL 2025 Britain's FCA [USN:L5N3QH0TT TEXT:"approves"] Shein's London IPO — but Chinese regulatory sign-off is still needed. MAY 2025 Shein [USN:L5N3RZ02P TEXT:"pivots"] to Hong Kong, [USN:L1N3RA0XL TEXT:"dropping"] its London-focused PR firms Brunswick and FGS in a sign the UK float is faltering. JULY 2025 The company [USN:L1N3SU0B2 TEXT:"files confidentially"] for a Hong Kong IPO. JULY 2026 China's CSRC approves Hong Kong IPO. AUGUST 2026 Shein launches its Hong Kong float. SEPTEMBER 2026 Shein will make its Hong Kong market debut on September 1. (SOURCES: Reuters stories and reporting, other media)
